subject.title: Feature Request: User-Level Skill Preferences/Conventions Support

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class per-skill user preference sidecar to the core skill loader, and what canonical contract should own it?
rationale: The request changes user-facing skill prompt semantics and adds a new preferences/config surface in the session context path, which repository policy treats as maintainer-owned product/API direction rather than a narrow bug repair.

options.title: Design a core preference contract
options.body: Keep this issue open and specify a canonical markdown sidecar or config-backed shape with precedence, refresh, prompt-version, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader skill selection work
options.body: Track this under a unified skill preference/priority/composition design if maintainers want one public contract for all skill-selection conventions.

options.title: Decline core sidecar loading
options.body: Keep preferences in full user skill overrides, `skills.entries.<key>.config`, or external skill/package guidance if maintainers do not want another core prompt-loading surface.

recommendation.title: Design a core preference contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and specify a canonical markdown sidecar or config-backed shape with precedence, refresh, prompt-version, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent routing signal across the current skill/config code and related maintainer discussion surface.
